question: Does URL-level pointwise mutual information (PMI) between actions and next-states detect predictive dynamical structure on real browser-collected SPA transitions when URL fragments are preserved — and how much information does standard fragment-stripping normalization destroy?
hypothesis: On TodoMVC hash-SPA variants where fragment-stripping normalization collapses all URLs to a single state (normalized URL entropy = 0.0 bits), raw URL PMI with fragments preserved will be significantly positive under cross-trajectory permutation testing, demonstrating that hash-based routing encodes state information in URL fragments that standard normalization destroys. The magnitude of raw-vs-normalized PMI difference directly quantifies the information loss from fragment-stripping. At least 3/5 variants will show raw URL PMI > 0.05 bits with Bonferroni-corrected permutation p < 0.01.
falsifier: The claim is falsified if ANY of: (1) fewer than 3/5 variants achieve raw URL PMI > 0.05 bits with Bonferroni-corrected permutation p < 0.01; OR (2) the positive control (synthetic deterministic SPA) fails (PMI < 1.0 bits); OR (3) fewer than 3/5 variants have >= 50 non-leakage transitions after filtering; OR (4) fewer than 3/5 variants have >= 5 unique raw URLs (insufficient state variation for PMI); OR (5) more than 1/5 variants have > 50% singleton state-action pairs (PMI estimator degenerate).
baselines: Normalized URL PMI (null representation baseline): PMI computed on URLs after fragment-stripping normalization. Expected to be exactly 0.0 bits on all TodoMVC variants because normalization collapses all URLs to a single state. This is not a statistical null but a mathematical identity — it validates that the PMI estimator correctly returns 0 when the state space is trivial.

Action-frequency baseline: P(action_type) marginal distribution across non-leakage transitions. Expected: form_submit ~33%, button_click ~23%, js_navigate ~17%, link_click ~0% (all link_click are leakage). If PMI equals action-frequency information without state conditioning, the effect is action-frequency, not state-dependent dynamics.

Achievable NL baseline: 50 NL transitions at 28% leakage (worst case) requires 69 raw; at 21% leakage (best case) requires 64 raw. All 5 variants previously achieved 108-130 valid non-error transitions at 168 raw, so 350 raw total (70 per variant) is sufficient.
positive_control: Synthetic deterministic SPA with 8 states, 4 actions, known action->next-state mapping (same as EXP-PHYSICS-34149195420). URL-only PMI must be >= 1.0 bits with permutation p < 0.001. This validates the PMI pipeline detects known structure in the SPA-like data format before testing real browser-collected data.
null_control: Normalized URL PMI on TodoMVC variants. Expected: exactly 0.0 bits (mathematically forced by fragment-stripping normalization collapsing all URLs to one state). Pass criterion: normalized PMI = 0.0 bits on all 5 variants. Any non-zero value indicates a pipeline bug.
measurement_validity: 5 TodoMVC hash-SPA variants: vanillajs, react, vue, angular, svelte (same as parent EXP-PHYSICS-35209110569).
Data source: reuse parent raw transition files (raw_{variant}.json and raw_{variant}_topup.json) from research/experiments/EXP-PHYSICS-35209110569/. No new browser collection required.

Non-leakage filter: action_primitive != 'link_click' (all link_click on TodoMVC hash-SPAs are leakage per parent audit V3). Alternative filter: action_target is None or action_target does not resolve to state_after URL.
Minimum 50 non-leakage transitions per variant (parent achieved 83-107 per variant).
Minimum 5 unique raw URLs per variant (parent achieved 3 after normalization; raw URLs with fragments expected to have 3+: #/, #/active, #/completed).
Session grouping: group transitions by session field to form trajectories for permutation testing.

Two PMI conditions: (A) raw URL PMI — state = raw url_before (with fragment); (B) normalized URL PMI — state = normalize(url_before) (fragment stripped). Both use same action and next-state representation.
Action representation: action_primitive categorical (form_submit, button_click, js_navigate). Link clicks excluded by non-leakage filter.
Permutation test: 1000 cross-trajectory shuffles of action labels within sessions, seed=42, Laplace alpha=1.0 for PMI smoothing.
Bonferroni correction: 5 primary comparisons (5 variants), alpha = 0.05/5 = 0.01.
decision_rule: If ALL of: (1) >= 3/5 variants achieve raw URL PMI > 0.05 bits AND Bonferroni-corrected permutation p < 0.01 AND (2) normalized URL PMI = 0.0 bits on all 5 variants (null control passes) AND (3) positive control PMI >= 1.0 bits AND (4) >= 50 non-leakage transitions per variant AND (5) >= 5 unique raw URLs per variant — verdict = SURVIVES_CURRENT_TEST (URL-level PMI detects predictive structure on real SPA transitions when fragments preserved). If fewer than 3/5 variants achieve raw URL PMI > 0.05 bits — verdict = FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING (URL-level PMI does not detect predictive structure on these SPAs even with fragments). If controls fail or data quality insufficient — verdict = MEASUREMENT_INVALID.
product_consequence_positive: Hash-SPA URL fragments encode state information detectable by PMI. SPIDER's URL representation should preserve fragments on hash-routed SPAs rather than stripping them. The synthetic-to-real gap is partially bridged: real browser-collected SPA transitions carry URL-level predictive structure. This justifies proceeding with PMI analysis at larger scale on these testbeds.
product_consequence_negative: Even with fragments preserved, URL-level PMI does not detect predictive structure on real SPA transitions. SPIDER should use richer state representations (DOM, accessibility tree, visual layout) rather than URL-only for SPA transitions. The synthetic-to-real gap persists: PMI pipeline detects structure on synthetic data but not on real browser-collected SPA data.
estimated_cost: Very low: no new browser collection (reuse parent raw data), Python analysis only (~1-2 hours). No model calls required.
expected_information_gain: Very high: directly tests whether URL-level PMI detects predictive dynamical structure on real browser-collected SPA transitions — the dominant synthetic-to-real gap across the C-WEB-DYNAMICS research program (30+ experiments). The raw-vs-normalized comparison uniquely quantifies information loss from fragment-stripping, a representation choice affecting all prior URL-level analyses. A positive result (raw PMI > 0) demonstrates real SPA transitions carry URL-level structure and justifies larger-scale PMI analysis. A negative result (raw PMI = 0) falsifies URL-only representation for SPAs and forces pivot to richer state representations. Either outcome resolves the dominant unknown with minimal cost.
